topics.topic: Capturing share of the RIA advisor market and evolving advisor-facing solutions
topics.stated_position: Management says advisor-facing solutions "must evolve" as the RIA value proposition shifts toward personalization, financial planning, behavioral coaching, wellness, and tax planning, and that Morningstar is "fully engaging here across our solutions," including UMA functionality, embedding the Risk Ecosystem in Morningstar Office, embedding sustainability offerings across all advisor-facing products, models, and a proprietary direct indexing pilot beginning in Q2 2022 with a select group of financial advisors.
topics.quote: As the value proposition of independent RIAs continues to shift toward areas like personalization, financial planning, behavioral coaching, wellness, and tax planning, advisor-facing solutions must evolve with respect to core portfolio management activities as well as these new areas of focus. We are fully engaging here across our solutions, integrating existing capabilities and developing new capabilities to address the changing needs of the investors they serve.

topics.topic: Creation of the Morningstar Wealth Management product grouping under Daniel Needham
topics.stated_position: Management describes uniting Managed Portfolios, Morningstar Office, ByAllAccounts, and Morningstar.com into a wealth management solutions product grouping, with the pending Praemium U.K./international acquisition also sitting within this group; the aim is "not" merely more advisors but "increasing the connectivity of our advisor solutions and increasing revenue per advisor."
topics.quote: While adding more advisors is important, our aim is to continue increasing the connectivity of our advisor solutions and increasing revenue per advisor as a result.

topics.topic: Competitive position of Morningstar's TAMP versus Envestnet and other larger TAMPs
topics.stated_position: Management believes its platform "is at parity with or exceeds the experience offered by many of our competitors," continues to invest, and cites being voted the number-one TAMP by advisors for service and performance in The Wealth Advisor's America's Best TAMPs, 2022 edition.
topics.quote: We believe our platform is at parity with or exceeds the experience offered by many of our competitors, and we continue to invest to enhance the experience.

topics.topic: Differentiation of personalized portfolios; proprietary data sets
topics.stated_position: Management points to independent research, proprietary data, and technology platforms, citing a proprietary direct indexing solution launching in beta in Q2 2022 combining Morningstar Sustainalytics metrics and Morningstar Indexes, and a new Target Date Plus service with Capital Group described as "a significant leap forward in the personalization of target-date funds."
topics.quote: We believe this is a significant leap forward in the personalization of target-date funds and will be appealing to investors.

topics.topic: Operating leverage and margins in the asset-based/Investment Management business
topics.stated_position: Management declines to provide forward guidance on margins but says it is experiencing positive operating leverage as products attract assets, excluding the impact of "the disclosed client losses that were a result of our strategy shift," and is focusing on growing AUM.
topics.quote: While we cannot provide forward guidance on margins, we are experiencing positive operating leverage as our products and investment strategies within Investment Management attract assets. That was indeed the case last year within Managed Portfolios, if we exclude the impact of the disclosed client losses that were a result of our strategy shift.

topics.topic: Loss of the TD Ameritrade relationship and remaining large Investment Management contracts
topics.stated_position: Management states the Managed Portfolios asset decrease from $48.6 billion in Q4 2019 to $23.1 billion in Q1 2020 is largely explained by the TD Ameritrade client loss, that TD Ameritrade switched to a fixed-fee arrangement as it transitioned the business in house and terminated the agreement following its merger with Charles Schwab, and that there are no remaining $10 million-plus clients in Investment Management revenue "as we shift away from consulting work to focus on direct relationships with advisors."
topics.quote: There are no $10 million-plus clients contributing to Investment Management revenue as we shift away from consulting work to focus on direct relationships with advisors.

topics.topic: Moving upmarket in Workplace/retirement plan managed accounts
topics.stated_position: Management says small and midsize plans have "traditionally been the sweet spot" but it has built out a direct-to-plan sales team for larger plans, a consultant relations team, a specialized engagement team, and is building a call center; it says the investment "has started to pay off," citing Raytheon as its most recent large plan win.
topics.quote: The small and midsize plan market has traditionally been the sweet spot for our managed accounts service. However, in the past few years we have built out the infrastructure to better serve and support larger plans.

topics.topic: Adoption of managed accounts as a QDIA
topics.stated_position: Management concedes it is "gaining traction and seeing increased interest but have not yet seen significant adoption" of managed accounts as a default option, particularly where recordkeepers have proprietary target-date funds they are encouraged to sell.
topics.quote: We are gaining traction and seeing increased interest but have not yet seen significant adoption of managed accounts as a default option in the plans we work with, especially when distributed by recordkeepers that that have proprietary target-date funds that they are encouraged to sell to plans.

topics.topic: Disclosure of Indexes revenue and possible reclassification of licensed data revenue
topics.stated_position: Management says Indexes revenue is not disclosed separately "as it has not reached the size of our 'top' product categories," confirms the investor's derivation is "within a reasonable range," and says it will consider reclassifying licensed data product revenue within Indexes to the licensed-based category in the future.
topics.quote: We do not currently disclose the Index revenue separately as it has not reached the size of our "top" product categories, but your derivation of Index revenue is within a reasonable range.

topics.topic: Justification for the price paid for Leveraged Commentary & Data (LCD)
topics.stated_position: Management says it focuses on overall cash returns and expects the acquisition "to generate strong returns well above our cost of capital," plans to enhance a core product that "hasn't been updated in years" and sell it to PitchBook clients, and notes the divestiture was triggered by regulatory requirements from S&P Global's IHS Markit merger; on competitiveness of the process it says "While the process was likely competitive, we ran our own race."
topics.quote: Through our extensive diligence and evaluation of how we will integrate LCD into Morningstar, we expect the acquisition to generate strong returns well above our cost of capital. We have significant opportunity to grow the product.

topics.topic: LCD growth profile, accretion, and planned investment
topics.stated_position: Management states LCD has experienced steady mid- to high-single-digit revenue growth, supported by "differentiated, hard-to-find data," that the transaction is expected to be accretive to adjusted net income per share in the first year after closing and to adjusted operating margins, and that it plans to invest behind the acquisition with much of that focused on integration into the PitchBook platform.
topics.quote: We have plans to invest behind the acquisition to support future growth, with much of that focused on integration into the PitchBook platform. We expect our integration efforts to include more substantial product development activity and greater emphasis and resources to expand the go-to-market approach.

topics.topic: Expected synergies from LCD across PitchBook, Indexes, and DBRS Morningstar
topics.stated_position: Management declines to quantify but says there are "significant opportunities" particularly within PitchBook and Indexes that were factored into expected returns, including better penetration of the addressable market, new investable products based on LCD data, cross-selling, and support for DBRS Morningstar credit analysts.
topics.quote: We believe there are significant opportunities across our business, particularly within PitchBook and Indexes, that were factored into our analysis and expected returns from the transaction.

notable_language.quote: While the process was likely competitive, we ran our own race.
notable_language.why_notable: An unusually colloquial and self-consciously disciplined framing of acquisition pricing discipline in response to a pointed question about paying 11-12 times sales.

notable_language.quote: we expect the acquisition to generate strong returns well above our cost of capital
notable_language.why_notable: Sets an explicit, recurring return standard management can be held to on the LCD deal, in place of any quantified financial detail.

notable_language.quote: as it hasn't been updated in years
notable_language.why_notable: A blunt characterization of an asset it just agreed to buy from S&P Global, framing the acquisition as a turnaround/enhancement opportunity.

notable_language.quote: There are no $10 million-plus clients contributing to Investment Management revenue as we shift away from consulting work to focus on direct relationships with advisors.
notable_language.why_notable: Confirms a strategic repositioning away from large institutional consulting contracts and away from the client-concentration model that produced the TD Ameritrade loss.

notable_language.quote: While adding more advisors is important, our aim is to continue increasing the connectivity of our advisor solutions and increasing revenue per advisor as a result.
notable_language.why_notable: Reframes the wealth management goal away from advisor count toward revenue per advisor — a shift in the stated success metric.

notable_language.quote: we have not yet seen significant adoption of managed accounts as a default option in the plans we work with
notable_language.why_notable: A direct admission that the QDIA thesis Morningstar has promoted has not yet translated into adoption, hedging a growth narrative.

notable_language.quote: That was indeed the case last year within Managed Portfolios, if we exclude the impact of the disclosed client losses that were a result of our strategy shift.
notable_language.why_notable: Positive operating leverage claim is expressly conditioned on excluding client losses management attributes to its own strategy shift.

notable_language.quote: The small and midsize plan market has traditionally been the sweet spot for our managed accounts service.
notable_language.why_notable: Candid characterization of the historic limits of the Workplace franchise, against which the stated move upmarket should be measured.
